newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GETRONICS FIRST HALF NET JUMPS 45 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: GETRONICS FIRST HALF NET JUMPS 45 PERCENT.

text.p: Dutch computer networks and engineering firm Getronics on Thursday reported 1997 first half net profits up 45 percent and said it expected continuing strong growth in net sales and profits for the rest of the year.

Net profits in the first half jumped to 79 million guilders from 54.5 million during the same period of 1996. The company saw turnover increase by 19 percent to 1.28 billion guilders while operating profits grew 18 percent to 107.8 million.
The increase in operating profit was generated by organic growth, the company said, adding it continued to see business conditions in the second half as favourable.
"The earlier published expectation of a continuing strong growth in net sales and earnings is therefore maintained," Getronics said in a statement.
The strong rise in earnings was partially attributable to good results from the group's RAET software unit, it said.
Getronics acquired the remaining 50 percent of shares it did not already known in RAET in December and said this had had a positive effect on the first half results.
Successful recruitment policy in the Netherlands had allowed the company to take full advantage of opportunities for growth, it said.
Getronics' activities in the area of software development and management grew by more than 25 percent in the first half, with project returns and fees increasing, the company said.

The group also won a large number of contracts for computer and network management during the period and further consolidated its leading position in the area of personnel information systems, it said.

The financial position continued to improve, the company said, with the solvency ratio after correction for cash increasing to over 48 percent and group equity growing to 335 million guilders, up 29 percent from the end of 1996.
Group net margin went up to 6.2 percent from 5.1 percent in 1996, Getronics said.
